target.name: Roam Robotics
target.founder: Tim Swift, Mallory Ulaszek, Saul Griffith

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $16M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Roam Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $16.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company operating in the robotics sector, including peers at similar and adjacent stages such as Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $16.4M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Series A to the next funding stage, yielding an implied valuation of $33M. The peer-median approach benchmarks against three same-sector comparables spanning Seed through Series B stages—Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, and Walden Robotics at $1.1B—producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B.

The triangulation of these two methods produces a valuation range of $28M to $1.9B, with a median of $841M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation multiples and the heterogeneity of comparable company scales. The peer-median approach carries greater weight given its grounding in recent market transactions, though the applicability of Series B and Seed comparables to a Series A target introduces stage-matching risk. Resolution of this range will depend on unit economics, revenue trajectory, and capital efficiency relative to the peer set.
